title: Sim-LLM: Optimizing LLM Inference at the Edge through Inter-Task KV Reuse
version: NeurIPS 2025 official proceedings PDF (current publisher bytes, checked 2026-10-21)
summary: The public Sim-LLM cache path can misassign tasks, rotate reused keys twice, duplicate a fresh cache and evict the wrong recency entry. Variable-length matching also has a known shape restriction.

problems.title: Cache insertion order does not preserve task identity
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF p.6; Algorithm 1, PDF p.25; modeling_llama_lsh.py, lines 120–171 and 1522–1535
claim: The matching loop is cache-first, while deletion and sequential reinsertion use current-batch indices. Neither sorted current indices nor unique current targets are enforced.
analysis: Matches \((0,1),(1,0)\) delete the first two current rows, leaving value \(12\). Insert cache value \(100\) at row \(1\), then \(101\) at row \(0\): output is \([101,12,100]\), while task-specific assignment requires \([101,100,12]\). Zero attention logits and constant row values transfer the same mismatch to the attention output. Single or correctly ordered matches can pass.
result: The released assembly can associate a task with another task’s values. Historical incidence is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Choose at most one cache entry per current task under a declared tie rule, then assign each final row by its original task index rather than insertion order.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local cache assembly failure without quantified central benchmark damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Already rotated keys receive another rotary transform
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF p.6; modeling_llama_lsh.py, lines 153–171, 753–782 and 2172–2197
claim: The traced producer stores post-RoPE keys; the consumer inserts those keys before applying RoPE to the assembled tensor.
analysis: At position \(p=1\), raw key \((1,0)\) is stored as \((\cos1,\sin1)\). Equal-position reuse should retain it, but the consumer returns \((\cos2,\sin2)\). A correspondingly rotated query changes its dot product from \(1\) to \(\cos1\). Position zero is a passing special case.
result: The producer/consumer representation contracts disagree. An unrotated-cache convention is a different contract.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Insert post-RoPE caches after rotating new keys. To move a cached key from position \(p\) to \(q\), apply \(R_qR_p^\top\) with trustworthy positional metadata.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public representation mismatch; original workload effects are unmeasured.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: A fresh target-layer cache is appended to itself
claim: `forward_predict_prompt` overwrites the incoming-cache variable with the current output, then concatenates its target layer with the same output layer.
analysis: With no incoming past and a three-token prompt, both operands are \((K,V)\). The target cache becomes \(([K;K],[V;V])\); a three-layer layout has lengths \((3,6,3)\) instead of \((3,3,3)\). The duplication occurs after initial hidden states are computed.
result: The returned generation cache is wrong for this fresh-prompt case. Nonempty-prefix behavior requires a separate accumulated-cache contract.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Keep the incoming cache under a distinct name and return the fresh target cache once. Append a prefix only where the documented backend returns new segments rather than already accumulated states.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded returned-cache bug, not proof that initial prompt logits or all benchmark scores are wrong.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Reference bits do not implement exact LRU
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF p.6; Appendix B.1, PDF p.23; Algorithm 1, PDF p.25; source lines 1544–1547 and 2214–2234
claim: The branch labeled LRU stores a reference bit and clears leading set bits rather than recording chronological recency.
analysis: For slots \([A,B,C]\), access order \(B,C,A\) leaves bits \((1,1,1)\). The code clears them and replaces slot zero, evicting most-recent \(A\); true LRU evicts \(B\). The same bit vector represents several different recency orders.
result: This is a different cache policy. No throughput advantage for exact LRU is established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Specify the reference-bit approximation, or maintain timestamps/an ordered recency structure and evict the actual oldest access under a deterministic batch convention.
problems.impact_rationale: The policy label differs from the public implementation; central performance impact is unknown.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Unequal prompt lengths fail the tokenwise matcher
claim: The matcher directly compares tokenwise cached and current embeddings without a common-length alignment contract.
analysis: Nonzero shapes \((1,2,2)\) and \((1,3,2)\) cannot broadcast across token dimensions \(2\) and \(3\). Equal padded widths avoid this failure, as in fixed-width settings, but do not solve general K/V alignment. Repository issue #1, opened 30 April 2026, already reported the concern.
result: This is a known public shape restriction, not a new discovery or a refutation of fixed-width experiments.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: A known interface limitation is preserved; no central fixed-width result is disproved.
problems.existing_correction_status: Repository issue #1 previously reported unequal-length failure; no complete variable-length correction or author adoption is established.
